beats.caption: The control gate is the top electrode of each cell
beats.text: On a NAND die, every cell has a control gate on top of its floating gate (or trap layer). The control gate sets the voltage that programs, reads or erases that cell.

beats.caption: Cut through: the control gate sits above the stored charge
beats.text: The control gate is a metal-filled poly plate. Between it and the floating gate lies the inter-poly dielectric, which lets the field from the gate reach the charge without leaking it away.

beats.caption: Word line: one row's control gates share one wire
beats.text: Control gates in a row connect along one word line. One voltage on that wire selects every cell in the row, so the controller programs or reads a whole page at once.

beats.caption: Read or program: the voltage on the gate sets the outcome
beats.text: A read puts a voltage on the word line and senses which cells conduct. A program pulse drives a higher voltage that pushes electrons in. The gate voltage, not the cell alone, decides what happens.

beats.caption: Makers: Micron (MU), Samsung (005930.KS), Kioxia (285A.T), SanDisk (SNDK)
beats.text: These four makers build NAND dies with control gates in this layout. Their word line wiring is what sets how many pages a die can address.
